findings.evidence: grep: `Convergence.lean:3-6` imports `Mathlib.Probability.Martingale.Basic`, `Mathlib.Probability.Martingale.Convergence`, `Mathlib.Probability.Process.Filtration`, then `Crossings.AntitoneLimit`; `AntitoneLimit.lean:3` publicly imports `Mathlib.Probability.Martingale.Convergence`; Mathlib `Convergence.lean:10` publicly imports `Upcrossing`, and `Upcrossing.lean:11` publicly imports `Basic`.
findings.fix: Drop the direct public imports on lines 3-5, or make only genuinely proof-local dependencies non-public if any remain after `shake`.
findings.issue: `Convergence.lean` publicly imports extra Mathlib modules even though `TauCeti.Probability.Martingale.Crossings.AntitoneLimit` already publicly imports `Mathlib.Probability.Martingale.Convergence`, which in turn publicly imports `Upcrossing` and `Basic`; this needlessly broadens the public import surface.

summary: The flagship theorem is now in the right module, but its wrapper still adds redundant public Mathlib imports that are already supplied by the imported implementation chain.
